title: Manufacture of sulphuric acid by contact process
topicTitle: Manufacture of sulphuric acid by contact process
notes: The contact process makes sulphuric acid from sulphur (or a metal sulphide), oxygen, and water.
Sulphur burns to sulphur dioxide: S + O2 → SO2. Dust and arsenic compounds are removed so they do not poison the catalyst.
The reversible oxidation is 2SO2 + O2 ⇌ 2SO3. Vanadium(V) oxide is the catalyst, at about 450°C and a pressure near 1–2 atm. The forward reaction is exothermic.
Sulphur trioxide is absorbed in concentrated sulphuric acid to form oleum, H2S2O7. Direct absorption in water produces a fine mist that is hard to condense.
Dilution of oleum gives the acid: H2S2O7 + H2O → 2H2SO4. A moderate temperature is a compromise: a lower temperature favours SO3 at equilibrium, but too low a temperature makes the catalyst slow.
